title: New York and Los Angeles restrict student AI as the technology becomes harder to avoid |
key_facts: On 2 Sep 2026 New York City announced a one-year moratorium on generative AI for students in pre-K to grade 8 for 2026-27.
High schoolers can use certain approved AI tools only under teacher supervision, and must complete two 45-minute AI-literacy lessons.
Los Angeles Unified placed a moratorium on AI on district-owned devices for the current school year but has no policy for personal devices.
Stanford's Victor Lee calls generative AI 'hard to disentangle' from ordinary tools such as Canva and PowerPoint.
Google announced on 25 June it was bringing Gemini in Classroom to students of all ages.
Education Week reported that schools had little time to decide how to monitor or restrict the technology.
quote_evidence: On September 2, New York City announced a one year moratorium on students facing generative AI for students in 2-K through 8th grade during the 2026-27 school year.
However, the moratorium applies specifically to district-owned devices, and they had not established a policy regarding students’ use of generative AI on their personal devices.
why_it_matters_hint: The two biggest US school districts restrict student AI but AI is built into everyday tools.
notes: Policies are from early September, older than 6 Oct; text appears to rely on Education Week. Score lowered by 1 as stale.
